Blaise Transit Launches On-Demand Transit in Prescott and Russell, Replacing All 12 Fixed Lines to Create a Fully on-Demand Transit Service Blaise Transit, a Canadian On-Demand Transit (ODT) provider,

paragraphs: Blaise Transit sells software for running transit without a fixed route or a fixed schedule. It was built to equip municipalities, cities, transit agencies, and transit operators. One platform covers demand-responsive service, paratransit, fixed-route integrations, and private shuttles.

The system comes in three parts. Blaise Engine lets operators set the vehicles, drivers, stops, and payment options that make up a transit system. A passenger app is available on Android, iOS, and as a website, where riders book, pay, and follow live vehicle locations. A driver app supplies turn-by-turn navigation on optimized routes and a passenger manifest at each stop. A separate simulations service recommends which transit models to implement and the parameters for each service.

Blaise was started in 2018 by a small group of transit-loving engineers. The site says more than 70 communities have chosen it to optimize their transit services. It reports working with agencies serving a few hundred rides a month up to a few million. Its optimization models are described as patent pending and customizable.
